headline: Nusrat murder: HC upholds death penalty for 2, acquits 10
summary: The High Court has confirmed the death sentences for two convicts in the brutal murder of Nusrat Jahan Rafi, while commuting four others' sentences to life imprisonment.
details: The High Court has upheld the death penalty for two individuals in the Nusrat Jahan Rafi murder case. Four other convicts have had their sentences commuted to life imprisonment, while 10 others were acquitted.
Nusrat Jahan Rafi, an Alim examinee, was tied up and set on fire on the roof of her madrasa in Feni's Sonagazi Islamia Fazil (Degree) Madrasa on April 6, 2019.
The murder was allegedly ordered by the former principal of the madrasa, Siraj Uddaula, lafter Nusrat had filed a complaint of sexual harassment against him in March 2019.
According to court documents and confessions, Nusrat was held down by five people on the roof, her hands and feet tied with her own scarf, and doused in kerosene before being set on fire.
Nusrat died five days later on April 10, 2019, while receiving treatment at the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
A lower court had previously sentenced 16 people to death in October 2019. The High Court's current ruling modifies these original sentences for several of the convicts.

headline_marked: 3 journalists [[sent to jail by ICT-2]] in crimes against humanity case
headline: 3 journalists sent to jail by ICT-2 in crimes against humanity case
summary: Shyamal Dutta, Mozammel Babu, and Farzana Rupa are detained following allegations of provocative remarks during the July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) has ordered three journalists to be sent to jail in a case involving crimes against humanity linked to the July Uprising.

The accused include Shyamal Dutta, editor of Bhorer Kagoj and former Jatiya Press Club general secretary, Mozammel Babu, former managing director and editor-in-chief of Ekattor TV, and Farzana Rupa, a principal correspondent for the same channel.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim alleged that during a press conference at Gono Bhaban on July 14, 2024, the journalists made provocative remarks.
The prosecution claims these remarks prompted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to refer to protesters as 'Razakars' and 'children of Razakars', which sparked widespread protests.
It is further alleged that the previously peaceful quota reform movement turned violent after attacks by Chhatra League and Jubo League activists on protesting students.
The defense counsel for Shyamal Dutta urged the tribunal to consider that there were no elements of crimes against humanity against his client before ordering the arrest.
caption:
Three journalists sent to jail by the International Crimes Tribunal-2 over allegations of provocative remarks during the July Uprising.

The International Crimes Tribunal-2 (ICT-2) has ordered three journalists to be sent to jail in a case involving crimes against humanity linked to the July Uprising.

The accused include Shyamal Dutta, editor of Bhorer Kagoj and former Jatiya Press Club general secretary, Mozammel Babu, former managing director and editor-in-chief of Ekattor TV, and Farzana Rupa, a principal correspondent for the same channel.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim alleged that during a press conference at Gono Bhaban on July 14, 2024, the journalists made provocative remarks.

The prosecution claims these remarks prompted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina to refer to protesters as 'Razakars' and 'children of Razakars', which sparked widespread protests.

It is further alleged that the previously peaceful quota reform movement turned violent after attacks by Chhatra League and Jubo League activists on protesting students.

The defense counsel for Shyamal Dutta urged the tribunal to consider that there were no elements of crimes against humanity against his client before ordering the arrest.
